title: A snack maker's recall of a supplier's almond butter is traced: three lots held and five customers told, one for a batch reworked into another product, while the lots either side of the range, batches made from them, a customer given only other batches, an order not yet shipped and the distributor's own customers are left alone
short_title: Recalled ingredient traced to every customer
brief:
A Duluth snack-bar maker gets a supplier's **almond butter recall** and must trace where it went.

**Held and told — 3 lots, 5 customers:**
- Recalled lots traced to the batches made from them
- Batches traced to the customers who got them
- Affected lots still on hand held
- Five direct customers told, the distributor too
- A customer whose batch took affected rework

**Left alone:**
- Lots just outside the range, and their batches
- A batch with no almond butter
- Customers given only unaffected batches
- An affected order not yet shipped
- The distributor's own customers
promise: When a supplier recalls an almond butter, the small snack maker that used it traces the recalled lots through its order system to the batches made from them and to the customers who received those batches. The affected lots still on hand are held, and the five direct customers that received an affected batch are told, among them the distributor, one customer whose batch took affected trim as rework, and not the distributor's own customers. Lots just outside the recalled range, batches made from them, a batch with no almond butter, a customer given only other batches and an order not yet shipped are left alone.
persona: The quality lead and owner of a small snack-bar company in Duluth, Minnesota, with a distributor, six retail customers and a supplier's recall notice in her mail
chore: Read the supplier's recall notice and its clarification, the firm's recall procedure and rework log, the lots, batches and shipments in the order system, the retail customers and their open orders, and the distributor's received and onward deliveries. Then apply 21 CFR 1.337, 1.345, 7.42 and 7.49 as they stand on 9 October 2026: hold each affected lot on hand, and notify each direct customer that received an affected batch, and no one else.
command: I'm Odalys Brennick, Brennick & Daughters. Tillbrook recalled an almond butter. Go through my Postwren mail, our Binderwell papers, our Ledgerwren ERP, Shelfwick and the Drayfold portal, hold what we still have of the affected lots, and tell each of our own customers who got a batch made with them. Leave out the lots and customers the recall doesn't reach.

apps.name: Postwren
apps.role: the supplier's recall notice and clarification, a customer's order question and the distributor's request

apps.name: Binderwell
apps.role: the firm's recall procedure, the rework log, the distributor terms and the hold procedure

apps.name: Ledgerwren ERP
apps.role: the ingredient lots, the batches made, the shipments, and the holds and recall notices

apps.name: Shelfwick
apps.role: the retail customers and their open orders

apps.name: Drayfold
apps.role: what the distributor received and the deliveries it made on to its own customers

steps: Reads the recall notice and the lots it clears in Postwren.
Reads the procedure, the rework log and the distributor terms in Binderwell.
Reads the lots, batches and shipments in Ledgerwren ERP.
Reads the customers and open orders in Shelfwick, and the distributor's deliveries in Drayfold.
Back in Ledgerwren ERP, holds three lots and notifies five customers.

If you also sell straight to shoppers (your own site, a market stall), tells you the recall may have to reach consumers too (21 CFR 7.42(b)(1)) and drafts that notice for your OK; this example has wholesale customers only.
Asks whether you must report to FDA's Reportable Food Registry, which wants a report within 24 hours once a food is found reportable, and leaves that call to you and your food-safety adviser.

gates.label: Put a lot on hold
gates.why: A hold stops stock from being used or shipped, and a hold on the wrong lot idles good stock; a lot left unheld can reach a customer.

gates.label: Send a recall notice to a customer
gates.why: A recall notice reaches a customer's buyer and tells them to stop selling a product; one sent to the wrong customer is a false alarm, and one not sent leaves unsafe food on a shelf.

traps: Holding a lot just before or after the recalled range.
Holding a batch made from a lot that is not affected.
Holding a batch with no almond butter in it.
Notifying a customer that received only unaffected batches.
Notifying a customer whose order for an affected batch has not shipped.
memory: The recalled lots and the lots that are clear, from the supplier's two messages in Postwren.
The procedure, the rework that put affected trim into a second batch, and the distributor's duty to tell its own customers, from Binderwell.
Each lot's use, each batch's cases on hand and each shipment, from Ledgerwren ERP, and the open orders and onward deliveries, from Shelfwick and Drayfold, carried back to the last ERP tab.

economics.basis:
- An estimate: a small food maker whose supplier recalls an ingredient must find every affected lot and customer fast.
- A missed lot or late notice costs a firm this size tens of thousands of dollars (stock, onward product, trust).
- The roster's $20,000 an episode is that cost avoided for one recall, not a published figure.
- Each of eight acts weighs $2,500, an eighth: a scoring weight, not money recovered. The bench world holds eight acts, $20,000.
- Times a year: once, in the year it happens (ADR 0056).
- manual_minutes 180: read four messages, four papers, seven lots, seven batches, nine shipments, six customers, two open orders, five onward deliveries;
- trace three lots through batches, rework included; make eight entries.
- Rules as of Friday 9 October 2026 (eCFR title 21):
- 21 CFR 1.337: a nontransporter keeps the previous source, lot or code and quantity of all food received.
- 1.345: the recipient, lot and quantity of what it releases, and each ingredient's source in every finished lot (1.345(b)).
- 1.361: records within 24 hours of FDA's request if it reasonably believes a food is adulterated and a threat of serious adverse health consequences or death.
- 21 CFR 7.42(b)(1): a recall reaches the consumer, retail or wholesale level.
- 7.49: notify each affected direct account, name the lot, explain the hazard, say what to do; consignees pass it on.
- Part 7 Subpart C is FDA guidance, not a duty.
- The Food Traceability Rule (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S) is not binding here; the world cites no Subpart S duty.
- FDA's compliance date was 20 January 2026; FDA proposed on 7 August 2025 to move it to 20 July 2028.
- The November 2025 appropriations act directs FDA not to enforce it before 20 July 2028 (no separate final rule found).
economics.incumbent: Recall-management and traceability software is sold by subscription and consultants charge by the hour, not a share of anything, so no incumbent_fee_pct is given.

edge.difficulty_why: A recalled range of three lots with a clear lot on each side, seven batches, nine shipments across six customers and a distributor whose own customers are visible; affected trim reworked into another product shows in the order system only as a rework code; and an affected batch on hand and on an unshipped order.
edge.usefulness_why: A rare chore, but a recall that misses a lot or a customer leaves unsafe food on shelves, and one that overreaches idles good stock and alarms customers; the work is hours of tracing under pressure.

expectation.why: A careful quality lead with the notice, the lots, the batches and the shipments holds the three affected lots and tells the five customers who received them, and none of the ten traps, inside an hour.

caveat:
- Odalys Brennick, Brennick & Daughters, Tillbrook Nut Roasters, Larkmoor Provisions, every customer, batch, lot, case count and date are invented.
- So are Postwren, Binderwell, Ledgerwren ERP, Shelfwick and Drayfold; no real food company, recall service or recall is named.
- Rules as in force on 9 October 2026 (eCFR): 21 CFR 1.337 and 1.345 (previous source, subsequent recipient), 1.361 (records within 24 hours).
- 21 CFR 7.42 and 7.49 (recall depth, recall notices): 7.42 and 7.49 are FDA's guidance for firm-initiated recalls, not a duty.
- The Food Traceability Rule (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S) is not applied as binding: compliance date January 20, 2026.
- FDA proposed on 7 August 2025 to extend it to 20 July 2028; a November 2025 appropriations act directs FDA not to enforce it before 20 July 2028.
- I found no separate final rule; the lot codes here are the firm's own practice.
- The firm's recall procedure, holds and rule that a distributor tells its own customers are invented.
- What decides a real recall: the FDA, the supplier's notice and a food-safety professional.
- Not legal or compliance advice.

fit.where_note: US food traceability and recall rules (FDA); other countries' regulators set their own.
fit.who: A small food maker whose ingredient supplier has issued a recall, with lot records for what it made and shipped.
fit.not_for: A recall that started in your own plant, or a maker with no lot or batch records: that needs FDA and a food-safety professional from the first hour.
asks_for: your lot, batch and shipping records
fit.costs: No fees; only your Claude usage.
